description:
## Why

Audit found integration tests in `pkix-path-builder/tests/integration.rs` cover only PKITS §4.1.1 happy-path topologies and the adversarial-budget stress test. None of the S/MIME stress patterns (bridge CA cross-cert, key rollover with same-DN-different-SPKI, TA name collision, multiple-valid-paths disambiguation) have integration coverage.

This means PKIX-yn3e (AKI selection) and PKIX-mszo (next-candidate iterator) ship with no regression-protecting test corpus. Filing this as a sibling so both can reference it.

## What

Build out integration test fixtures and tests covering:

1. **Bridge CA cross-cert with AKI disambiguation** — pool with two intermediates sharing issuer DN but different SPKIs; target's AKI uniquely identifies one. Test that AKI-aware selection (PKIX-yn3e) finds the verifying path on first DFS pass, and that without AKI handling the wrong candidate is selected first.
2. **Key rollover (old-key signs new-key cert)** — pool with old-key root + cross-cert from old-key root to new-key. Target signed by new-key. Verify both topology layers are walked correctly.
3. **TA name collision** — anchors set with two trust anchors sharing DN but with different SPKIs. Pool builds a chain whose terminal cert's issuer DN matches both anchors. Verify that `build_path` returns one path and `validate_path` succeeds against the matching anchor.
4. **Multiple-valid-paths disambiguation** — pool admits two same-length valid paths to anchors. Document the deterministic tiebreak (pool-insertion order today; AKI-preference once PKIX-yn3e lands). Test the contract.
5. **CMS-bag-shaped pool** — irrelevant context certs in pool (other-CA intermediates, expired self-signed, EE certs from unrelated chains). Verify the builder finds the right path through the noise.
6. **Three-cert loop A→B→C→A** — verify cycle guard terminates without hitting the budget (currently the audit notes loop detection is correct but only stress-tested via the 30-self-loop budget test, not a true 3-cycle).

## Acceptance

- [ ] At least one fixture per stress pattern committed under `pkix-path-builder/tests/fixtures/`. Generate via openssl with explicit AKI/SKI extensions where needed; document the generation script for reproducibility.
- [ ] Integration tests covering each pattern, asserting both the topology returned (via `build_path`) and the end-to-end verdict (via `validate_path`).
- [ ] When PKIX-yn3e and PKIX-mszo land, these tests demonstrate the new behaviour. Until then, tests can xfail-style document the current limitation.
- [ ] No additional runtime deps. `std` may be used (this is dev tooling).

## Out of scope

- Real-world bridge-CA cert fixtures (those involve government PKI roots that are heavyweight to vendor in-tree). Synthetic openssl-generated fixtures are sufficient for the topology tests.
- pyca / x509-limbo integration as test source (that's PKIX-g9vc).

## Filed as

S/MIME-in-production audit follow-up. Provides regression coverage for PKIX-yn3e and PKIX-mszo.
notes: Decomposed 2026-05-10 into 7 child beads (PKIX-xj81.1 shared infra + PKIX-xj81.2 through .7, one per stress-pattern topology). Each topology depends on the shared infra. Epic blocked on all children closing. Decomposition rationale: 6 fixture topologies with OpenSSL-crafted AKI/SKI extensions is a high-blast-radius task that benefits from focused, individually-reviewable beads rather than one large undifferentiated commit. PKIX-xj81.1 is the only currently-ready child; topology beads (.2 through .7) unblock when .1 closes.
title: pkix-path-builder: bridge CA / cross-cert / TA collision integration test corpus
